note:
FEATURE / TESTING ARCHITECTURE ISSUE: Revamp repository validation so every production change is tested at both the owning-module level and the assembled-game level, with all visual acceptance performed through the real standalone-player build/capture harness.

REQUIRED VALIDATION MODEL: For a production change: (1) run focused automated tests owned by the changed module; (2) if the module has player-visible output, run its module-local validation scene through the standalone-player build/capture harness; and (3) run `KentridgePlayableSlice` through the standalone-player harness as the canonical top-level game integration/smoke gate.

PLAYMODE IS NOT VISUAL PROOF: PlayMode tests may validate behavior, state, geometry, traversal, contracts, or other runtime semantics, but PlayMode-rendered screenshots are not valid visual acceptance evidence. Any assertion that something visually looks correct must use frames rendered by the built standalone application. Existing PlayMode screenshot tests may remain as diagnostics or behavioral regressions where useful, but they cannot satisfy a visual acceptance gate.

MODULE-OWNED VALIDATION SCENES: Player-visible modules should own small, deterministic validation scenes alongside the module rather than adding feature-validation scenes to the top-level `Assets/Scenes` area. For example, Water should own a scene showing representative still water, shallow shoreline, river flow, waterfall, and terrain-contact cases; structural composition should own representative structural/socket compositions; terrain rendering should own representative terrain cases. These scenes exist specifically to make the owning module easy to inspect and must exercise the real production implementation rather than parallel test-only rendering code.

MODULE SCENE LOCATION: New module validation scenes belong beneath or alongside their owning module/test area rather than the top-level game-scene directory. They do not need to be shipping game scenes or permanently present in normal player build settings. The shared harness must be able to build the requested validation scene directly.

ONE VISUAL HARNESS: There must be one shared standalone-player build/capture mechanism used for module-local visual scenes, `KentridgePlayableSlice`, and SceneIssue visual replay. Do not create module-specific player harnesses. The generic harness must not contain feature-specific knowledge such as mappings from particular test class names to scenes, automatic TownArchitecture/water/castle/Kentridge audit selection, hard-coded feature-specific cameras/walks/screenshot counts/timing based on scene name, or other silent decisions about what proves a feature. Feature/module-owned configuration should explicitly declare the scene/scenario to execute; the harness should only build, launch, drive the declared scenario, capture presented frames, and report success/failure.

MODULE TESTING RESPONSIBILITY: Focused EditMode/PlayMode tests remain the fast local regression layer. A changed module should have a deterministic way to identify its owned focused tests. The architecture should make the expected module test set explicit rather than forcing agents to infer it from unrelated test names or global showcase suites.

KENTRIDGE INTEGRATION GATE: `KentridgePlayableSlice` is the canonical assembled-game integration gate for production changes. It must build and launch as a real player and exercise enough normal gameplay/world generation to detect startup/runtime exceptions, broken world generation, missing or incompatible module integration, traversal/collision failures, rendering/shader failures, and other major regressions visible only when systems are composed. Module validation proves the component itself; Kentridge proves the component still works in the game.

DECLARATIVE VALIDATION TARGETS: Replace implicit harness selection with explicit validation declarations. A SceneIssue/module validation request should be able to declare focused tests, zero or more module-local built-player visual targets, and the canonical Kentridge built-player integration target. Scene and scenario are separate concepts: the scene identifies where validation runs; the scenario identifies cameras, movement, timing, captures, and assertions. The runner is shared infrastructure and must not infer a scenario from test class names or scene names.

CURRENT ARCHITECTURE TO SIMPLIFY: The current validation path contains special-case mappings between PlayMode test names and scenes, special-case Kentridge evidence behavior, and scene-specific visual audits inside the generic player capture path. This issue should remove or migrate those feature-specific decisions into explicit module/scenario-owned declarations rather than adding another parallel testing path.

AGENT WORKFLOW: Update `AGENTS.md`, SceneIssue workflow instructions, CI request semantics, and any relevant validation documentation so agents are told exactly which declared validation targets to execute. Agents must not be expected to choose, invent, or extend an unrelated harness to prove their feature. Remove stale or conflicting workflow references encountered during the migration, including references to non-existent validation documentation.

MIGRATION PROOF: Demonstrate the architecture by migrating at least one representative player-visible module, preferably Water, to a module-local validation scene and proving the complete flow: focused module tests -> built-player module visual validation -> built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` integration. The migrated visual scene must use the production module implementation and its visual proof must come only from the standalone-player harness.

ACCEPTANCE:
(1) A clear repository convention maps production modules to their focused automated tests and, where applicable, module-local validation scene/scenario.
(2) Player-visible modules can own validation scenes beneath/alongside their module rather than placing all validation scenes in top-level `Assets/Scenes`.
(3) The standalone-player harness can build and capture an arbitrary declared module validation scene without requiring test-name-to-scene inference or permanent normal-build registration.
(4) All visual acceptance uses standalone-player output. PlayMode-rendered screenshots or RenderTextures may remain diagnostic but cannot satisfy a visual acceptance gate.
(5) Every production-module validation path includes focused module tests plus the canonical built-player `KentridgePlayableSlice` integration gate.
(6) Player-visible modules additionally run their module-local visual scene/scenario through the same standalone-player harness.
(7) Remove or migrate generic-harness special cases that infer feature-specific audits, camera behavior, timing, screenshot requirements, or scenes from test names/scene names. Required behavior belongs in explicit module/scenario declarations.
(8) Scene and scenario are represented separately enough that multiple validation targets can use the same shared runner without embedding feature policy in shell/CI infrastructure.
(9) Update `AGENTS.md`, SceneIssue workflow instructions, CI request semantics, and relevant validation docs so agents run declared targets rather than choosing a harness. Remove stale references such as `SceneIssues/feature-readme.md` if it remains absent.
(10) Preserve exact-SHA CI/evidence requirements and fail when a declared focused test, module scene, built-player capture, or Kentridge integration gate does not actually execute. A zero-match test or skipped configured target cannot count as green.
(11) Migrate at least one representative visual module, preferably Water, to a module-local validation scene and prove the exact flow `focused module tests -> built-player module visual validation -> built-player Kentridge integration`.
(12) The migration does not create a second standalone-player harness, module-specific build implementation, or another parallel CI transport.
(13) Existing useful focused regressions remain available, but visual acceptance semantics are removed from PlayMode-only evidence paths.
(14) The resulting architecture is simpler to explain than the current system: module tests prove the module contract, module-local built-player scenes prove player-visible output, and built-player Kentridge proves assembled-game integration.
(15) Measure CI/runtime cost and keep the architecture suitable for routine agent iteration; do not make every focused iteration pay for unnecessary visual scenarios, while final production validation must execute all required declared gates.
